label: FP
reason: Both alerts are structural false positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) and Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) share the same data flow where user input 'param' enters an ArrayList, is shifted by removing the first element, and then retrieved at index 1. Due to the initial addition order ['safe', 'param', 'moresafe'], removing index 0 leaves ['param', 'moresafe']. Retrieving index 1 yields the constant "moresafe". Thus, the resolved sink value for both SQL execution and HTML printing is a constant string, excluding user input.

evidence.note: List construction adds "safe", "param", "moresafe"; remove(0) eliminates user input; get(1) retrieves constant "moresafe".
SQL sink executes query built from "bar", which resolves to constant "moresafe".
XSS sink prints encoded "sql", which resolves to constant "moresafe".
